newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rail strikers end strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rail strikers end strike.

text.p: Workers at Croatian state railways (HZ) said on Tuesday they would end a three-week-old strike after the Supreme Court confirmed that the stoppage was illegal, state media reported.
Some 11,000 workers of the loss-making HZ went on strike on November 28. They stopped all passenger and cargo trains to press demands for higher wages and better working conditions.
HZ said it was losing $300,000 daily due to the strike and risked being unable to pay the workers' November wages.

The Supreme Court ruled last week the stoppage was illegal, but the strikers appealed against the decision. The court rejected the appeal on Tuesday, state radio said. Strikers said earlier they would comply with the latest ruling.
The main rail workers' trade union released a statement on Tuesday saying "the strike is called off, in line with two decisions of the Supreme Court", the state news agency HINA reported.
Under pressure from the government and HZ management the strikers had already resumed passenger traffic on December 4. Less than a week later they restarted a skeleton cargo service.
During the strike the government, faced with a wave of popular protests, stood firm and said there was no money to increase pay this year.
Croatian Railways (Hrvatske Zeljeznice) is a state-owned company, and the government is expected to spend more than one billion kuna (some $200 million) in 1996 alone for its subsidy.
